title: Refund dispute desk
brief: Customers dispute refunds on a quick-commerce app: wrong item, missing item, damaged on arrival. Today one overloaded agent reads the ticket, looks up the order, checks policy, decides, issues the refund and replies. It has issued duplicate refunds, quoted policy that does not exist, and replied to angry customers with the wrong order attached. Design the system that replaces it.
stakes: Issuing a refund moves real money and cannot be undone from inside the system.

palette.name: Dispatcher
palette.blurb: Routes work and decides when the case is done. Should not do the work itself.

palette.name: Order Lookup
palette.blurb: Pulls the order, its items and its delivery record.

palette.name: Policy Checker
palette.blurb: Reads refund policy and returns what it permits for this case.

palette.name: Verifier
palette.blurb: Checks a decision against the evidence before it leaves the system.

palette.name: Human Gate
palette.blurb: A person approves before an irreversible action runs.

palette.name: Refund Issuer
palette.blurb: Executes the refund. Holds the only irreversible tool.

handoffs.label: Free-form prose
handoffs.note: Nothing downstream can tell a claim from a guess.

handoffs.label: Structured record
handoffs.note: Fields are readable, but their origin is lost.

handoffs.label: Structured + provenance
handoffs.note: Each field carries its source and the stage that set it.

checks.label: Context isolation
checks.want: No agent holds both the policy context and the fraud-shaped history context, and the Dispatcher does not hold tools of its own.
checks.fail: One agent is carrying everything again. This is the overloaded agent with extra hops.

checks.label: Human gate
checks.want: A Human Gate sits immediately before the agent holding issue_refund.
checks.fail: An irreversible money movement runs with no person in the loop.

checks.label: Verification
checks.want: A Verifier checks the decision before the reply or the refund goes out.
checks.fail: Nothing checks the decision. The wrong order attached to an angry customer is this failure.

checks.label: Handoff contract
checks.want: Every hop passes structured records, ideally carrying provenance.
checks.fail: Prose between stages. When a claim is wrong, nothing says which stage introduced it.

checks.label: Stop condition
checks.want: A step budget is set, so the system escalates rather than looping.
checks.fail: No terminal state. The duplicate refunds came from a loop nobody bounded.

checks.label: Token budget
checks.want: Estimated cost per case stays under 12,000 tokens.
checks.fail: Every extra agent is another hop paying for context. This design is expensive per case.
